Definition: from G4862 and G4137; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete):--(fully) come, fill up.
BiblicalUsage: When the day of Pentecost was fully come, the disciples were all with one accord in one place, and the Spirit fell. Luke uses the same word for the time come for Jesus to be received up, when He set His face to go to Jerusalem, and for the boat filling with water in the storm on the lake. A time can be filled up, a boat can be filled up, and the filling is the moment when what was promised arrives.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that God's times come fully, not partly, and Pentecost proves it: when the day was fully come, the Spirit came. I hold that the same God fills my times, and I can trust Him to bring them to their full measure. And I take courage from the boat too, because the One who fills the time is the One asleep in the storm.
